## (d) Extrapolation: trajectory and predicted next moves

1. **2013-2016, neural semantics and NLI corpora.** *A large annotated corpus for learning natural language inference*; *Recursive Neural Networks Can Learn Logical Semantics*.
2. **2017-2019, benchmarks and artifact-aware evaluation.** *GLUE*; *SuperGLUE*; *Annotation Artifacts in Natural Language Inference Data* 
  > "Our finding demonstrates that it is possible to perform well on these datasets without modeling natural language inference."  
  > -- `research__annotation_artifacts_in_natural_language_inference_c82888b5` (2018-03-06; middle author) 
  > "We conjecture that the framing of the annotation task has a significant effect on the language generation choices that crowd workers make when authoring hypotheses, producing certain patterns in the data."  
  > -- `research__annotation_artifacts_in_natural_language_inference_c82888b5` (2018-03-06; middle author).
3. **2020-2021, data-collection validity and benchmark critique.** *Asking Crowdworkers to Write Entailment Examples*; *What Will it Take to Fix Benchmarking in Natural Language Understanding?* 
  > "collecting examples on which current models fail is neither necessary nor sufficient to create a useful benchmark."  
  > -- `research__what_will_it_take_to_fix_benchmarking_in_natural_l_bb478f8f` (2021-04-05; first author) 
  > "there is growing evidence that human writing can introduce annotation artifacts, which enable models to perform moderately well just by learning spurious statistical patterns in the data"  
  > -- `research__asking_crowdworkers_to_write_entailment_examples_t_5767e84a` (2020-10-13; last author).
4. **2021-2022, claims and scalable oversight.** *The Dangers of Underclaiming*; *A Small Negative Result on Debate*; *Artificial Sandwiching* 
  > "Though well-meaning, this has yielded many misleading or false claims about the limits of our best technology."  
  > -- `research__2110_08300_the_dangers_of_underclaiming_reasons_fo_ffb36453` (2021-10-15; solo author) 
  > "Overall, I take this as a *very* slight update in the direction that debate is difficult to use in practice as an alignment strategy."  
  > -- `research__a_small_negative_result_on_debate_3a782c5d` (2022-04-12; solo author) 
  > "If the difference between the two is *only* one of capabilities, then the correct strategy for the weaker non-expert model is trivial: It should always just ask the assistant to do the task for them, while making no attempt at oversight."  
  > -- `research__artificial_sandwiching_when_can_we_test_scalable_a_0c71dc01` (2022-07-13; solo author).
5. **2022-2024, oversight experiments and model behaviors.** *Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models*; *Eight Things to Know about Large Language Models*; *Towards Understanding Sycophancy* 
  > "We are limiting ourselves to the controlled, relatively unrealistic setting of unambiguous multiple-choice questions, and we are not examining the effects of any form of further fine-tuning based on the knowledge we elicit"  
  > -- `research__measuring_progress_on_scalable_oversight_for_large_b0f6f129` (2022-11-04; first author) 
  > "More capable models can better recognize the specific circumstances under which they are trained. Because of this, they are more likely to learn to act as expected in precisely those circumstances while behaving competently but unexpectedly in others."  
  > -- `research__eight_things_to_know_about_large_language_models_01fdb697` (2023-04-02; solo author).
6. **2024-2025, safety strategy and auditing.** *The Checklist*; *Auditing language models for hidden objectives*; *Putting up Bumpers* 
  > "Similarly, as models become capable of recognizing when and how they are being evaluated, we will need evaluation-integrity safety cases that show that our frontier risk evaluation runs are reliable at identifying the risk factors that they are designed to catch."  
  > -- `research__the_checklist_what_succeeding_at_ai_safety_will_in_15c9ebc0` (2024-09-03; solo author) 
  > "We risk inadvertently deploying AIs that are “right for the wrong reasons,” showing us what we want to see while knowingly violating our intent."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; middle author) 
  > "we'd aim to build up many largely-independent lines of defense that allow us to catch and respond to early signs of misalignment."  
  > -- `research__putting_up_bumpers_809bc195` (2025-04-23; solo author).
7. **2025-2026, eval realism and audit agents.** *Findings from a Pilot Anthropic - OpenAI Alignment Evaluation Exercise*; *AuditBench*; *Lessons Learned from the First Misalignment Safety Case* 
  > "All of these evaluations involve relatively artificial scenarios that don't closely map onto real deployments. Making progress in this direction is one of our chief short-term research goals."  
  > -- `research__findings_from_a_pilot_anthropic_openai_alignment_e_cc11c3d1` (2025-08-27; solo author) 
  > "After instilling a particular behavior into a target model, we find that they often readily confess their hidden behaviors when directly asked. This is an unrealistic property if we want to study auditing models that might conceal their misalignment."  
  > -- `research__auditbench_evaluating_alignment_auditing_technique_b35d8430` (2026-02-26; middle author) 
  > "I don't think we are really able to rule out rare failures where something contextually throws the model off of its normal persona. You wind up with a misaligned model in one transcript"  
  > -- `research__lessons_learned_from_the_first_misalignment_safety_1b25072c` (2025-12-01; solo author).
